headline: Chips Lead a Broad Advance as Oil Stays Hostage to Middle East Headlines
body_html:
Wall Street approaches Thursday's open with Wednesday's rally still fresh. Of the 668 stocks we track, 461 rose and 202 fell, and semiconductors did the heavy lifting with a 5.9% jump, well ahead of every other group. Pre-market quotes are thin at this hour and not a dependable guide, so the first question is whether chip buyers show up again.

Energy was the second-strongest group, up 2.87%, as crude recovered from an early drop on geopolitical worries. Reports of missiles intercepted over Saudi Arabia and Iranian attacks on shipping navigation equipment near Oman keep oil sensitive to overnight news. Software gained 1.22%, financials 1.08%, healthcare 0.98% and industrials 0.96%, while consumer stocks were nearly flat. Homebuilders were the weak spot, down 1.35%.

At the open, watch the leaders for follow-through or profit-taking: Azenta climbed 20.8%, Applied Optoelectronics 15.6% and Sandisk 13.69%. On the downside, Tetra Tech fell 7.48%, the session's steepest drop. Any fresh Gulf headline could swing energy and the broader tone quickly.

briefs.headline: Crude Rebounds After Early Slide
briefs.body: Oil pared an early decline and moved higher as geopolitical risks supported prices. Energy shares were Wednesday's second-best group, up 2.87%. Traders will watch whether the bid holds as Thursday's session opens.

briefs.headline: Saudi Air Defenses Intercept Houthi Missiles
briefs.body: Saudi Arabia said it shot down missiles and drones launched by Houthi forces, and that debris fell in the Mecca region. The group denied aiming at the holy city. The episode adds to the regional risk premium traders are weighing.

briefs.headline: Iran Accused of Hitting Navigation Systems at Omani Island
briefs.body: Sources say Iran attacked shipping navigation equipment on Oman's Didamar island. Any disruption to maritime routing is a concern for energy flows and insurers, and it is one more reason oil may react sharply to overnight news.

briefs.headline: Tehran Seeks Compensation at Climate Summit
briefs.body: At the COP31 climate talks, Iran said it wants payment for environmental damage from US and Israeli strikes. The demand is unlikely to move markets directly, but it shows how entangled the diplomatic backdrop remains.

briefs.headline: Apple's Record Run Draws Heavy Options Activity
briefs.body: Apple's climb to record territory has set off a flurry of options trading, a sign investors are positioning around the big-cap leader. Watch whether that activity carries into the open and how it affects the broader technology tone.

briefs.headline: Meta Infrastructure Chief to Depart
briefs.body: Meta's head of infrastructure is leaving, and a former cloud executive from Amazon's AWS unit will take over. The change comes as spending on computing capacity is closely watched across the technology sector.
